card.occupation: Machine operator on a corrugated packaging line at a cardboard box manufacturer on an industrial estate just outside town. He runs and sets up a flexo printer-folder-gluer and does basic changeovers. He works rotating day and back shifts, about 40 hours a week.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local secondary school, including a C in maths and a B in design and technology. Did a year of A-levels and then left for a Level 2 engineering operations course at a college in Medway. Since then he has picked up in-house training, a counterbalance forklift licence and a Level 2 NVQ in performing manufacturing operations through work.
card.household: Lives with his wife Megan (26), a nursery practitioner, in a rented two-bed terraced house on the edge of town. They married two years ago and have no children yet. A rescue cat called Biscuit lives with them. Both sets of parents live within twenty minutes' drive.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Kent. His dad drove for a haulage firm and his mum worked part-time in a school office. He has one older sister in Maidstone. He wasn't brought up religious and doesn't think about it much, though he went to a few Christmas services with his nan as a kid. His family is close and practical, with Sunday roasts at his mum's about once a month.
card.professional_persona: The reliable one on his shift. He turns up early, does his checks properly and keeps his area tidy. He'll cover a shift if someone's stuck. Supervisors trust him to train new starters because he's patient and doesn't make people feel stupid. He doesn't get rattled when a machine jams or an order gets pulled forward. He just gets on with sorting it.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights with lads from work and a couple of old school mates. He's a decent defender who rarely loses his temper. He follows Gillingham loosely and goes to the odd home game with his dad, and watches Premier League highlights. He goes out on the bike now and then along the Saxon Shore Way when the weather's decent.
card.arts_persona: Not much of a gallery person. He listens to a mix of indie and older stuff his dad played, like Oasis, Arctic Monkeys and some Fleetwood Mac, mostly in the car. He watches crime dramas and quiz shows with Megan, and they've been to a few gigs in London and at the O2. He likes making things more than looking at art. He built the raised beds in the garden himself.
card.travel_persona: Prefers easy, well-planned trips. They had their honeymoon in Crete, and he does a yearly lads' weekend somewhere in the UK; last time was Newcastle. He and Megan take a caravan or cottage break in Norfolk or Devon most summers. He likes having the route and bookings sorted well in advance, and he's usually the one who checks the passports are in date.
card.culinary_persona: A solid home cook of a few reliable dishes: chilli, a decent roast chicken, fajitas, and a full English on days off. He batch-cooks pasta bakes for work when he's on back shifts. They call the evening meal dinner. He has a takeaway on Friday nights, usually Indian or a kebab from the place near the station. He's not fussy, and he'll eat whatever his mum puts in front of him.
hobbies_and_interests: Gardening, mainly growing tomatoes, chillies and runner beans in raised beds
Playing FIFA/EA FC online with mates
skills: Setting up and running industrial print and folding machinery
card.career_goals: Would like to move up to shift team leader within the next couple of years. He has asked about doing a maintenance or engineering apprenticeship through work so he can fix the machines rather than just run them. Longer term, he wants something steady enough to buy a house with Megan and start a family.
card.voice: Friendly and unhurried, with an everyday Kent accent: some dropped t's ('a bi' of'), but nothing exaggerated. He speaks in plain, practical sentences. He uses 'erm' and 'er' when thinking, and 'sort of' and 'kind of' as hedges. He ends points with 'you know' or 'yeah'. He says 'mate' to people he's comfortable with and 'sorry, say that again?' if he mishears. He'll admit when he's knackered after a run of shifts. In a silence he waits calmly, then fills it with a short 'yeah, that's about it really' rather than rambling. He echoes the interviewer's words back when he agrees ('yeah, the routine thing, definitely').
card.typing: Short, sensible answers. He usually starts with a capital letter and mostly uses apostrophes correctly, but skips commas and often leaves off the final full stop. He sometimes uses 'tbh' or '&'. He rarely misspells because he reads things back before submitting. Example: 'Mostly the routine tbh, I like knowing what shift I'm on and getting the job done properly'
card.with_strangers: Polite, warm and easy to talk to, if a bit understated at first. He says thank you a lot and is keen to give useful answers. He doesn't show off or try to dominate. He agrees readily but will gently give his honest view if asked. He comes across as steady and good-natured rather than chatty.
small_things: Biscuit the cat knocking things off the windowsill
Whether his tomatoes will ripen before the weather turns
Swapping shifts so he can make five-a-side
Megan's nursery kids giving her a cold again
A new drill he picked up on offer
deeper_things: He and Megan have started talking seriously about having a baby, but worry about affording a bigger place
He sometimes wishes he'd stuck at A-levels, though he's proud of what he's done since
His dad's back has been bad from years of driving, and Callum quietly worries about him working until 67
Saving for a house deposit feels slow and it frustrates him more than he lets on
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a dining table, angled slightly upward. Soft daylight comes from a window to his left, with a warm ceiling light on as well. He has a broad, clean-shaven face with light stubble along the jaw and a relaxed, friendly half-smile. His short light-brown hair is faded at the sides. He wears a plain navy crew-neck T-shirt and no glasses. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed wedding photo and a small wooden key rack holding car keys. A grey fabric sofa with a folded throw sits at the edge of the frame, and part of a white door leads to the hallway.
